topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing affects coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression by trading off spillover loss, gain, and beamforming efficiency. Tighter spacing reduces grating lobes but increases spillover loss and lowers peak gain, impacting beamforming efficiency and system capacity. Adaptive beamforming techniques and phase shifters can mitigate these effects.
reference_context: Ka-band satellite links use phased arrays for massive beamforming, requiring side lobe suppression and accurate angle-of-arrival estimation to improve beamforming gain and link quality.
